name: The Kelp Labyrinth
layout: Iron-hard kelp stalks rise from the muddy floor to the surface in narrow mazes; ordinary kelp is cut with the Survival Knife, Iron-Kelp needs the Heated Blade. Clearings hold copper, quartz and titanium nodes; the tangled dreadnought hangs here.
look: Shadowy emerald water, sunbeams filtered through the canopy, floating spores, dark shapes between giant rubbery trunks.
hazards: Propeller tangles, very low visibility, and ambush predators disguised as kelp fronds (Wraiths, the Tangle-Serpent Leviathan).
foodWeb: Iron-Kelp, other macro-algae and phytoplankton feed plankton, sluggish grazers (Kelp-Cow, Kelp-Grazer Manatee, Holdfast Hog) and armoured snails. These feed stalkers like the Stalker-Hound and Lancer Pike and suction hunters like the Suction-Maw Eel. Scavengers led by the Root-Marrow Worm recycle fallen kelp. The Tangle-Serpent Leviathan and Shroud Serpent ambush anything big that displaces water.
source: The Deep Design Document.pdf, The ten ecosystems (flora and fauna tables) and Featured species

interactions: Noisy, bleeding or propeller-driven crews attract the whole chain; the serpents strike anything big that displaces water.
The Tangle-Serpent Leviathan hangs motionless among the kelp and wraps any sub passing within 15 m; at the dreadnought it hides its 95 dB constriction roar in the ship's metal groans.
Stalker-Hounds stalk divers rather than attacking at once, stealing dropped tools and titanium scrap and caching the loot in hollow kelp roots.
Moss-Nibbler Wrasse clean parasites off resting Kelp-Grazer Manatees; Holdfast Gleaner Shrimp clean wounds on resting fish.
Stalk Urchin herds gnaw holdfasts, toppling stalks and opening new clearings.
Kelp-Stripe Orca pods echolocate through the maze and herd prey into clearings.
Pod-Cracker Bream crunching pods gives feeding groups away to predators.
Glimmer Mysids flash blue when disturbed, revealing nearby divers.
Bulb-Lure Anglers mimic Glow Bulbs to ambush Bulb-Picker Gobies and careless collectors.
Tangle Dogfish hunt by smell in packs of five and frenzy at blood; Carrion Whelks and Silt Brittle Stars converge on blood and kills within minutes.
Gasp Tubeworm bubble bursts briefly mask nearby noise; Strangle Spongeweed slowly kills kelp stalks.
Lubricants leaking from the tangled dreadnought confuse predators' sense of smell, hiding a diver's blood trail.
